meta.target_definition: Each nowcast is the model's forecast of the BEA advance estimate of annualized real-GDP growth, evaluated the day before the advance release (the pre-advance cutoff). At that cutoff the target quarter's GDP is still unobserved and BEA same-day co-releases (real PCE, income, PCE prices, durable goods) are excluded, so the score is a genuine pseudo-real-time forecast error with no look-ahead leakage. The macro-only dynamic factor model is the 'Staff Nowcast' (a standard central-bank-staff DFM); the 'Fiscal-enhanced DFM' adds a fiscal block (federal deficit, government spending, income excluding transfers).

comparison.convention: A=fiscal, B=baseline; loss_diff=loss_fiscal-loss_baseline; loss_diff<0 and dm_stat<0 => fiscal more accurate; horizon h=1

power_mde.method: For h=1 the DM-HLN statistic equals the ordinary paired t-test, so MDE = (t_{1-alpha/2,df} + t_{power,df}) * SE(d), df=n-1, SE(d)=sd(d)/sqrt(n) with sd(d) the unbiased sample SD. This central-t formula is the standard approximation to the exact noncentral-t MDE (here within ~0.02%, and if anything slightly conservative). Squared-loss effects are in MSE units; the RMSE-scale equivalent is RMSE_base - sqrt(MSE_base - effect).

benchmarks.convention: Headline target = BEA advance annualized real-GDP growth at the (advance-1) cutoff. DM: A=DFM, B=benchmark; loss_diff=loss_dfm-loss_bench; loss_diff<0 and dm_stat<0 => DFM more accurate; horizon h=1.
benchmarks.gdpnow_note: GDPNow excluded: no clean ALFRED point-in-time vintage history exists for the Atlanta Fed GDPNow series, so a faithful pseudo-real-time (advance-1) replay is infeasible; a non-real-time splice would leak future revisions and is not honest.

fiscal_impact.convention: Impact = (Actual - Forecast) * Weight, summed |.| over the weekly vintages of a quarter for the fiscal-block series. gain = |error_StaffNowcast| - |error_FiscalEnhanced| (>0 => fiscal block helps). signed_deficit = signed Impact of MTSDS133FMS (the GDP-nowcast revision from deficit news; >0 => bigger deficit pushed the nowcast up). resid_vs_staff = realized advance growth - macro-only Staff Nowcast (the non-circular axis for the signed scatter). summary.signed reports Pearson r+p of signed_deficit vs {growth=realized, resid=realized-staff}, pre/post/all, with the post-COVID OLS fit and a decomposition_post block (deficit/macro/residual cross-corrs). Pre-COVID <=2019, Post-COVID >=2021, 2020 excluded.

ablation.convention: Headline (advance-1) ex-2020 (n=30). Each model = the shared macro panel plus the listed fiscal series, on the same US_fiscal data with the DFM re-estimated. dm_vs_macro / dm_vs_all are DM-HLN (h=1) loss-differential tests of this model against the macro-only Staff Nowcast and against the all-three model (A=this model, B=ref; dm<0 => this model has lower loss). Source: ablation/run_ablation.py.

findings.title: The fiscal block helps more often than not
findings.body: Ex-2020 the Fiscal-enhanced DFM edges the macro-only Staff Nowcast on both scores -- RMSE 2.06 vs 2.15 pp, MAE 1.45 vs 1.52 pp -- and is more accurate in 19 of 30 non-COVID quarters (10/18 post-COVID). The edge is modest and concentrated after 2020, not a clean sweep of every quarter.

findings.title: The signal is the deficit, and it switches on post-COVID
findings.body: The fiscal block's news (Impact = actual - forecast, weighted) is 5.0x larger post-COVID than before, and where it is larger the Fiscal-enhanced DFM gains more accuracy over the Staff Nowcast (correlation 0.45 post-COVID, 0.51 after controlling for error size). The effect is carried almost entirely by the federal deficit (corr 0.38); government spending and income excluding transfers add essentially nothing. Pre-COVID the fiscal news was tiny and unrelated to accuracy (corr 0.04).

findings.title: Suggestive, not yet statistically established
findings.body: On formal testing the fiscal edge is real-but-fragile: it is significant only on MAE ex-2020 (DM -2.2, p=0.036), not RMSE (DM -1.54, p=0.134); over all 34 quarters the two are indistinguishable. That one significant cell sits below its minimum detectable effect (|effect| 0.071 < MDE 0.094) and a single p=0.036 across four tests does not survive multiple-testing correction. On 34 quarters the story is economically coherent but underpowered.

findings.title: Factor models are far more robust in the tails
findings.body: Over all 34 quarters both DFMs are dramatically more robust than the traditional univariate benchmarks, which blow up on 2020: Staff Nowcast RMSE 5.59 vs random-walk 13.32 and AR(1) 11.61. The multivariate factor structure keeps the nowcast from chasing a single series off a cliff -- the main edge of the DFM family over traditional models.

findings.title: No precision edge over naive models in calm times
findings.body: Ex-2020 neither DFM beats the traditional benchmarks on RMSE: Staff Nowcast 2.15 vs historical-mean 1.96 and AR(1) 2.08. The naive models are tighter but biased (mean bias +0.58, AR1 bias +0.59); the DFMs trade a little noise for near-zero bias.

findings.title: DFM vs traditional: a statistical tie on this sample
findings.body: None of the 16 DFM-vs-benchmark Diebold-Mariano tests (0/16 reject at 5%) are significant: by formal testing the factor models and the traditional ones are statistically indistinguishable on this short 34-quarter sample. The DFM's real value is robustness in the tails plus the weekly within-quarter path it produces, not a headline-RMSE win in calm times.

findings.title: Honest pseudo-real-time target
findings.body: Every nowcast is scored against the BEA advance growth estimate at a pre-advance cutoff (advance day minus one). No target value and no same-day BEA co-release leak into the forecast, so the errors below are genuine, not read-backs.

findings.title: 2025q1 miss is genuine, not leakage
findings.body: 2025q1 is a contaminated quarter: on the advance day BEA co-releases real PCE (~68% of GDP), real income and PCE prices. The (advance-1) cutoff excludes all of them, so the large 2025q1 miss is a true forecast error, not a leakage artifact. Only 4 of 33 past quarters are fully clean across the whole release week.
